equity_bridge.item: Equity investments at fair value / carrying value
equity_bridge.note: Q2 FY2027 10-Q balance sheet (2026-09-30); income from these sits below operating income and is outside the flows, so the asset is added (matching-asset rule). Includes 70-ish of listed stakes; the remainder is private and would be haircut by a buyer.
Definitive agreement, ~$265M cash, expected to close around end of Q2 FY2027 subject to regulatory approval; the cash is still on the 2026-09-30 balance sheet so the commitment is deducted here.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Year-1 (FY2027) base-case growth anchored on reported H1 FY2027 (+25%) and Q3 FY2027 guidance ($1.54B, ~+24%) with a tougher Q4 comparison; not the equity CAGR, which is inflated by SBC credited to paid-in capital (see warning).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 26.9% is 45% above EPS 3yr CAGR 18.6%. The divergence is mechanical: ~$2.9B of cumulative SBC since FY2024 is credited to additional paid-in capital, so book value compounds faster than the business earns. Equity CAGR is therefore NOT a conservative growth anchor for Arm and was not used.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs are undefined because the owner-FCF series is negative in each of FY2024-FY2026 (reported FCF 998 / 178 / 979 less SBC incl. employer taxes 1,246 / 1,044 / 1,212 less interest income 110 / 116 / 111). Reported FCF grew 13.2%/yr over 3 years while SBC incl. employer taxes grew from 326 (FY2023) to 1,212 (FY2026), i.e. all of the reported FCF growth and more has been paid for in stock. Revenue history starts FY2022 (earliest filing), so 5-year revenue/EPS CAGRs are null and 4-year figures are given instead; the FY2021 equity figure (4,050) does exist, so the 5-year equity CAGR is genuine.

scenario_narratives.base: Arm's royalty annuity keeps compounding mid-teens as hyperscaler Arm share exceeds 60%, Armv9/CSS lift royalty per chip and the Q2 FY2027 licensing surge (+50%) turns into royalties over 2-5 years, while mobile (43% of royalties, >99% share) is flat-to-low-growth. The Arm AGI CPU delivers roughly the guided up-to-$2B of FY2027-28 silicon revenue at hardware margins, which dilutes the pre-SBC EBITDA margin to ~46% for two years before the IP mix restores ~49%. The valuation axis that matters most is SBC: at 29% of revenue incl. employer taxes in year 1 the house (owner-FCF) basis is only modestly cash-generative today, and the base case needs SBC to fall to ~14% of revenue by FY2036 for owner-FCF margins to reach the low 20s. Even then, intrinsic value is a small fraction of the current price -- the market is paying for the street (SBC-as-non-cash) convention plus a multi-year silicon option this model does not credit.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI data-center compute becomes Arm's largest end market: Neoverse/CSS share of hyperscaler silicon keeps rising past 60%, the AGI CPU grows into a multi-billion-dollar line through Meta, OCI and follow-on hyperscaler orders (well short of the ~$15B ambition management has floated), automotive/robotics scale, and the licensing boom of FY2026-27 feeds royalties in the early 2030s. Operating leverage on the IP franchise pushes pre-SBC EBITDA to 52% and SBC drifts to 11% of revenue as headcount growth lags revenue. Revenue reaches ~$22B by FY2036. Even this path, discounted at 10.5%, does not reach the current price on a fully SBC-expensed basis.
scenario_narratives.bear: The in-house-silicon pivot triggers the channel conflict Arm's own risk factors describe: large licensees hedge with RISC-V and architecture-licence in-house cores, royalty-rate uplift stalls after the Qualcomm/Nuvia litigation sets a precedent, Arm China (~16-18% of revenue) and tightening US/UK export controls on Neoverse V-series erode PRC revenue, and a hyperscaler AI-capex pause hits the fastest-growing royalty stream. Growth fades to mid-single digits by FY2030, production silicon stays a low-margin, inventory-bearing line that holds pre-SBC EBITDA at 44%, and SBC remains above 20% of revenue because Arm must keep paying up for engineers as growth slows. Owner-FCF margins top out in the low-to-mid teens and intrinsic value is near the net-cash-plus-modest-annuity floor.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF with SBC (including employer taxes on SBC) fully expensed and the diluted share count held flat, interest income stripped because the $3.6B net cash pile is added back in the bridge, a 10-year component build because owner-FCF margins are still ramping from roughly break-even, and a single 10.5% USD WACC with risk carried in the scenario paths and 25/50/25 weights. The headline is the house basis; the street basis (SBC as non-cash) is reported as the upper bound of the accounting-regime band so the reader can see how much of the market price rests on treating ~$1.4B/yr of compensation as free.
key_risks_to_valuation: SBC trajectory: the base case assumes SBC incl. employer taxes falls from ~29% to 14% of revenue by FY2036; every 1pp of terminal SBC is roughly 1pp of terminal owner-FCF margin
Production silicon (Arm AGI CPU) margin, inventory and foundry risk -- a hardware business grafted onto an asset-light IP model; the $2B FY2027-28 guide is management's, not a signed-revenue figure
Customer concentration and channel conflict: top five customers ~57% of revenue; licensees now compete with Arm's own chips
RISC-V and architecture-licence in-house cores capping royalty-rate uplift; Qualcomm/Nuvia litigation (trial Q4 CY2026)
Arm China (~16-18% of revenue) collectability and US/UK export controls on Neoverse V-series to the PRC
AI capex cycle: data-center royalties doubled YoY and are the fastest-growing stream; a hyperscaler capex pause hits the most richly valued driver first
Governance: SoftBank 86.4% control, CEO also part-time CEO of SoftBank Group International; minority ADS holders have no say
Terminal-value dominance: a 10-year build on a business whose owner-FCF margin is still maturing leaves most of the value in the terminal year

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API regular close at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 100.02-452.70
data_sources.financials: ARM_Metrics.csv (core_metrics from SEC 10-K FY2024-FY2026 and 10-Q through Q2 FY2027); FY2026 10-K for SBC/employer-tax/capex/D&A/interest/tax lines; Q2 FY2027 10-Q (2026-09-30) for cash, short-term investments, equity investments and diluted shares
data_sources.qualitative: ARM_Analysis.json (2026-11-08): business model, moat, growth drivers, risks, Q3 FY2027 guidance and AGI CPU commentary

inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted-average diluted ordinary shares, Q2 FY2027 10-Q (quarter ended 2026-09-30), 1 ADS = 1 ordinary share. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows (incl. employer taxes), so compounding the count as well would charge the same cost twice. No buybacks have ever been made, so the flat count is a modelling convention Arm has not yet paid for in cash.
inputs.cash_note: Cash and cash equivalents 3,251 + short-term investments 370 at 2026-09-30 (Q2 FY2027 10-Q balance sheet). Zero borrowings. Equity investments (599) are carried separately in equity_bridge.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K: share-based compensation cost 1,052 (cash flow statement, line 4218) plus employer taxes related to share-based compensation 160 (staff costs note, line 6507) = 1,212 -- the two lines Arm itself excludes from non-GAAP operating profit, so this is the company's own combined figure (GAAP operating income 900 + 1,212 = 2,112 ties to the 2,115 non-GAAP operating profit KPI). The 529 of cash tax withholding on net-share settlement (financing outflow, FY2026) is NOT added on top: those withheld shares were already expensed at grant-date fair value, so paying their tax in cash substitutes for dilution already charged.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD discount rate. Risk-free 4.2% (10y UST), equity risk premium 5.0%, fundamental beta 1.25 for a net-cash semiconductor-IP franchise (the post-IPO regression beta of ~2.5-3 is a liquidity/float artefact of SoftBank's 86% holding, not a cost of capital) -> ~10.5% cost of equity = WACC with zero debt. One WACC across all three scenarios; business risk is charged through the scenario paths and weights, not a second time through the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Leases stay in the flows: US GAAP operating lease cost is inside opex and therefore inside the EBITDA margin. Lease liabilities are $28M (FY2026 10-K line 5982), immaterial, and are NOT added to net debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: None -- no non-controlling interests. Arm China is an equity-method/royalty counterparty, not a consolidated subsidiary.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route (dcf-methods routing table row 1: operating company, tech/IP licensor). Fresh build -- no prior DCF, no memory entry. FY0 = FY2026 (year ended 2026-03-31, revenue 4,920); year 1 = FY2027, with H1 FY2027 (revenue 2,732, +25%) and Q3 FY2027 guidance (1.54B +/- 50M, ~+24%) already reported. OWNER FCF FY2026 is NEGATIVE: reported FCF 979 less SBC incl. employer taxes 1,212 less net interest income 111 = -344. The 160 of employer taxes is cash-settled inside OCF, so a strict no-double-count owner anchor is -184; the forward build is internally consistent because the EBITDA margin is the company's pre-SBC, pre-employer-tax non-GAAP basis (FY2026: (2,115 + 249 D&A) / 4,920 = 48.0%) and the SBC % path charges both lines. Interest income stripped because net cash (3,621) is many multiples of the FCF base. FY2026 capex (545, 11.1% of revenue) was data-center/office expansion and hardware per the 10-K (line 3019) and is ramped down, not carried forward. Working capital is a drain on growth for Arm (contract assets and receivables on upfront-recognised licensing exceed deferred revenue; FY2025 and FY2026 OCF were both well below net income + SBC + D&A), so wc_capture_pct is NEGATIVE. The two revenue economics are modelled through the blended paths: royalty (53%, recurring, Armv9/CSS rate uplift and data-center share) is the steady compounder; licensing (47%, lumpy, +50% in Q2 FY2027) and the new Arm AGI CPU production silicon (up to $2B cumulative FY2027-28, hardware margins, inventory) drive the near-term growth spike and the early-year margin dilution. Street-basis values add back the SBC charge and are the memo, not the headline.

bear.growth_rationale: FY2027 still +17% on the half already banked and the Q3 guide; from FY2028 the AGI CPU channel conflict costs licensing goodwill, RISC-V and architecture-licence in-house cores (the Qualcomm/Nuvia pattern) cap royalty-rate uplift, Arm China/export controls erode the ~18% PRC revenue, and AI capex pauses. Revenue ~$8.7B by FY2036. SBC stays sticky at 20%+ because engineering talent competition persists while revenue growth slows.

base.growth_rationale: FY2027 +20%: H1 +25%, Q3 guide ~+24%, Q4 against a 1,490 licensing-heavy comp implies ~+10% for ~5.9B. FY2028 +20%: the bulk of the up-to-$2B AGI CPU silicon lands plus mid-teens royalty growth (data-center share >60%, Armv9/CSS rate uplift). Then decelerates 16/14/12/10 as mobile (43% of royalties) stays flat-to-low-single-digit and data-center share gains mature, to 4% by FY2036.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-SBC EBITDA 48.0% in FY2026 (51.3% FY2025, 48.6% FY2024). Dips to 46% in FY2028-29 as low-margin production silicon enters the mix, then recovers to 49% as high-incremental-margin royalties outgrow silicon. SBC incl. employer taxes 24.6% FY2026 but 31.8% in H1 FY2027: year 1 at 29%, then -2pp/yr early (silicon revenue carries little SBC per dollar; headcount growth slows from +15%/yr) to 14% by FY2036 -- still above the mature-tech ~10-12% norm. Cash tax 20% (FY2026 cash taxes 223 on pre-tax 1,157 = 19.3%; UK patent box) ramping to 23% as the patent-box benefit dilutes under the 25% UK statutory rate. Capex 9% in FY2027 (H1 ran 9.8%) easing to 4.5% = D&A at maturity. WC capture -10% of the revenue increase: contract assets and receivables grow faster than deferred revenue.

bull.growth_rationale: AGI CPU becomes a multi-billion silicon line (management's public multi-year ambition toward ~$15B is NOT assumed; roughly $4-5B by FY2031 is), hyperscaler Arm share passes 60% and keeps rising, Q2 FY2027's +50% licensing surge converts to royalties 2-5 years out, automotive/robotics add a third leg. Revenue ~$22B by FY2036 (4.6x).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the house 15/50/35 default to 25/50/25. Bear weight up: top-five customers are ~57% of revenue (Arm China alone ~16%), the AGI CPU is an unproven pivot into a capital-intensive business that competes with those same customers, SoftBank's 86.4% control and the CEO's dual SoftBank role are a governance overhang, and the Qualcomm/Nuvia trial lands in Q4 CY2026. Bull weight down: the bull case needs several independent things to go right at once -- sustained hyperscaler AI capex, silicon execution with no licensee retaliation, continued royalty-rate uplift, and SBC falling by more than half as a share of revenue.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
